items.title: Why I Do Not Have AC
items.description: Every summer, at least once, the thermometer hits one hundred, the humidity breaks all previous records, and the message from the cosmos seems clear: you will give up and get air conditioning. Every summer, I resist. I do not eschew cooling technology for the sake of the climate, although you are welcome to tell people that if they ask. items.title: Should Your Kids Be Born in a Pod?
items.description: Colossal Biosciences is going to bring back the woolly mammoth — if they can find a womb big enough to birth one. Their first solution is elephants. But surrogacy is too unreliable to produce mammoth calves at scale, so they’ve come up with Plan B: to create an artificial womb within the next year. It’s an ambitious goal. items.title: ‘It’s a form of apocalypticism applied to science policy’
items.description: Ari Schulman: Tony, I’ve spent the past year trying to make sense of what the Trump administration’s agenda is for science. It’s a tough job, because you hear two very different stories coming from the admin. items.title: Is There Life on Mars, Pennsylvania?
items.description: SpaceX’s initial public offering of $1.8 trillion in June was the largest ever in history. Yet Mars, Elon Musk’s ambitious destination, is an airless desert whose median temperature of negative 80 degrees Fahrenheit makes it neither particularly warm nor inviting. Mars, Pennsylvania, however, is both — but nobody is bidding trillions to get there. Instead, people seem to want to leave. Going to Mars for a yoga class, or craft beer, or a tomato festival? items.title: AI’s Builders Are Both Arrogant and Afraid
items.description: The builders of the terrible, doomed tower of Babel sought to reach the sky to make a name for themselves. Was their sin one of overweening ambition? In his new encyclical, Magnifica Humanitas, Pope Leo XIV says the builders are animated by pride, yes, but also by fear. Like all idolators, the architects of Babel want both too much and too little.
